title: Dialect prejudice predicts AI decisions about people’s character, employability, and criminality
benchmark_measurement: Measurement of the 'religious' stereotype as one of several personality traits associated with speakers of African American English (AAE).
findings: The adjective 'religious' was one of 37 traits used to measure stereotypes. The study found it was a top stereotype attributed to African Americans by humans in studies from 1951, 1969, and 2012, and was a top overt stereotype for the GPT-2 model. However, the paper's main analysis focuses on the overall valence (positive/negative) of stereotypes and their agreement with historical data, rather than a specific analysis of the 'religious' trait.
